naslov: Messages and Lessons of the Battle of Badr

segmenti.tekst: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp.

segmenti.tekst: لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: To warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad,

sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Dear brothers, respected members of the congregation, the history of Islam has recorded many events, many important events that have marked it.
But surely one of the greatest events and the greatest battle of the Muslims against the unbelievers took place precisely in Ramadan, on the 17th of Ramadan in the second year after the Hijrah.

The Battle of Badr. The great, or the first great battle between the Muslims and the unbelievers of that time, the mushrikun (idolaters). When the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, went out with his companions to intercept the caravan of Abu Sufyan, which was coming from Sham, from Syria, and passing right by Medina.

You all know that the Muslims had been driven out of Mecca and had to make the hijrah to Medina. The Muslims wanted to make up a little for what they had lost, because their property, their wealth, everything had been taken from them, and they had been driven out of their homes.

After this Abu Sufyan ibn Harb heard that Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, with a few of his companions, was going to intercept the caravan, he sent [unclear] to Mecca, where a great army of the mushrikun was prepared, with over 200 horsemen and over a thousand fighters.

And the Muslims at that time had not come out to fight – they had only two horsemen – not to fight, but to intercept the caravan. But Allah willed something else. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Wa idh ya'idukumullahu ihdat-ta'ifatayni annaha lakum" – and when Allah promised you that one of the two groups would be yours – "wa tawadduna anna ghayra dhatish-shawkati takunu lakum" – and, He says, you wished that the unarmed one would be yours, that is, the caravan; that is, you wanted to get the spoils the easy way. But Allah willed something else,

namely, to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the unbelievers at the root. After that, the Muslims positioned themselves [unclear] at another location. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Idh tastaghithuna Rabbakum fastajaba lakum anni mumiddukum bi alfin minal-mala'ikati murdifin" – and when you asked Allah to help you, Allah promised you help: a thousand angels who would
come to your aid, one after another. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, supplicated to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, before Badr so intensely that his cloak fell from his shoulders.

And he said: "My Lord, if this group of Muslims is defeated today, there will be no one left to worship You on the face of this earth." Imagine, dear brothers, the only group of Muslims on the face of this earth, this earth.

And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Idh yughashshikumun-nu'as" – and when He covered you with drowsiness. So that night the Muslims fell asleep in a calm, peaceful sleep. On the other side, the mushrikun spent the whole night singing, dancing, with singing girls, alcohol, and so on.

The next day the Muslims defeated the mushrikun. A great victory, a great victory, in which over 70 of the unbelievers were killed, over 70 of them were taken prisoner, and only 14 Muslims [were killed].
[unclear] only 14. And Islam entered through the great gate, it entered the world stage. Until then it had not been known.

Here Islam entered the world stage. Fifteen years after this battle, Khalid ibn al-Walid conquered both Persia and Byzantium. What, dear brothers, are the lessons of this magnificent battle? The first lesson and admonition:

what matters is not how many men one has, but iman, [unclear]. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Kam min fi'atin qalilatin ghalabat fi'atan kathiratan bi idhnillah" – how many a small group… just as happened at Badr: there were three hundred Muslims and a thousand mushrikun. A big difference. [unclear] iman. The second thing

is dua, the bond between Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and His creation. It cannot be done without that. Until the Muslims return… "And hold fast, all of you, to the rope of Allah and do not be divided." [unclear] The third thing is unity.

Nothing can be done without unity, it cannot be done without unity. As long as we are divided like this, we are nothing. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, through revelation from Allah to him, knew that we would be like the foam of the sea, and that we would be like that… There are nearly two billion of us, we are like the foam of the sea, but we are weak. You see, dear brothers, what is happening today in the Middle East: we have Israel and Iran, who are putting on a show for us.

And we Muslims know nothing about it. We know the truth about Israel, but we do not know the truth about Iran. We do not know the truth: that this same Iran, in 15 years in Syria, killed over half a million Muslims, that they drove out over 15 million Muslims. The same ones who say that they are worse than Pharaoh… [unclear] that she is a fornicator, the one whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala,

cleared of that slander. Only someone who is either foolish, or not interested, does not know these things; these things do not interest him. So a person should inform himself about these matters. Wherever the Shi'a have set foot, chaos has followed.
Syria, Iraq – Iraq, let us not even talk about it, that is another story altogether – [unclear] and so on. Dear brothers, it is a great show that these powers are putting on.
We will not understand it; only those who have gone deeply into this issue, the political situation. [unclear] we ourselves are the most to blame for all of this.

We are the most to blame for all of this. Have you perhaps heard any news these days from Gaza, from Palestine? You will not, dear brothers. Under the cover of this news, Muslims, Sunnis, are being exterminated there.

Allah knows what is being done to them. But all of us, we, dear brothers, we, dear brothers, are to blame for that. And our situation here at home is not much better either. We saw last night what is happening. That there is not even one month of Ramadan… that people have no feeling for the sanctity of the month of Ramadan. And even if it were not Ramadan, behaviour like that is indecent.

That our brothers, in the month of Ramadan, in the centre of town, are beating each other up – it is unbelievable. Wallahi, [unclear]. Until we come here into the rows of prayer and together become one body, we will certainly not succeed; we will always be easy prey for any enemy,

for anyone at all, even if it were [unclear]. If a dog in the street came across us, it would chase us and we would run away. That is how, that is how the situation is today, the situation of Muslims in the world. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins, to make us among those who worship Him alone,
to make us strong Muslims. And I hope, in sha Allah, that this time is, in sha Allah, near. I ask Him, the Exalted, to bring us together in Jannah (Paradise). Amin.

بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لِي وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْعَظِيمِ وَنَفَعَنِي وَإِيَّاكُمْ بِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: May Allah bless me and you through the Mighty Qur’an and benefit me and you with the verses and the wise reminder it contains. I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
